paragraphs: Rabbi Shimon, son of Rabbi Abbahu.

Bereshit Rabbah 18:5 mentions Rabbi Shimon, son of Rabbi Abbahu. Hyman identifies the source of the passage as Jerusalem Talmud Yevamot. In the corresponding passage, Yevamot 11:2, the reading is “son of Rabbi Aivu,” and Rabbi Hila answers Shimon’s objection.

notes.text: The Bereshit Rabbah locator פ״יחדה remains unresolved. Abbahu and Aivu are the two supplied father-name readings.

The saved whole Torat Emet BereshitRabbah18:5 explicitly names Rabbi Shimon son of Rabbi Abbahu and then Rabbi Levi replying. Supplied פ״יחדה remains visible beside that matching locator, rather than a proved glyph repair. Hyman attributes son of Aivu and Hila’s resolution to Yevamot1:2; that paragraph was not newly inspected, so those abbreviated titles stay R'. The two father readings and differing respondents are not harmonized. Hyman owns the source-priority claim and the antecedent of his statement remains open.

The supplied transcription has פ״יחדה and gives Yevamot chapter 1, halakhah 2. Hyman’s printed notice (vol. III, p. 1156) gives a hyphenated chapter 18, section 5 reference for Bereshit Rabbah and appears to give chapter 11, halakhah 2 for Yevamot. The Guggenheimer text at 11:2 names Rabbi Shimon son of Rabbi Aivu, who asks about Amram and Yocheved. Rabbi Hila answers there. Bereshit Rabbah gives the father as Rabbi Abbahu and Rabbi Levi speaks next. Hyman’s claim about which work is the source remains his judgment.
